title: The Kitchen of Junebug Creek
premise: Ada Oyelaran inherits Junebug Creek Orchard from the grandmother she barely knew—along with a mortgage she cannot pay and a deed that lists a second name: Elias Marchetti, the boy she loved and abandoned ten years ago. Forced into an unwilling partnership to save the orchard from a developer's offer, Ada and Elias rebuild the kitchen where their history was made, and Ada must finally speak the apology she has rehearsed for a decade before the bank's deadline forces a sale. In the end, they choose each other and the orchard, refinancing together and reopening the kitchen as a supper club where memory becomes a living thing.
about_author: Paloma Lockridge is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded midnight shifts in restaurant kitchens for midnight shifts at the writing desk. She writes love stories set in places where food and grief share a table.

chapters.title: What the Lawyer Left on the Table
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In Atlanta, Ada learns her estranged grandmother has died and left her half of Junebug Creek Orchard—mortgaged to the hilt. The other half belongs to a name she hasn't spoken in ten years. Emotional beat: dread disguised as practicality; she almost refuses the inheritance outright.

chapters.title: The Second Name on the Deed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She drives to Junebug Creek and walks the overgrown orchard, finding the old kitchen intact and a man repairing its roof: Elias, older, harder, furious. He refuses to sell to her or with her. Emotional beat: the past arrives all at once, and neither can look away.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The bank gives them ninety days to refinance or the developer buys the land. Elias, who stayed and tended the orchard through his own losses, resents Ada's return but cannot abandon the trees. Emotional beat: resentment braided with the stubborn hope he thought he'd killed.

chapters.title: A Recipe in Her Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cleaning the kitchen, Ada finds her grandmother's recipe journal—entries that mention her by name, and Elias too, revealing the old woman orchestrated their reunion. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal, then softening into a question: why would Gran want this?

chapters.title: First Frost, First Harvest
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A late frost threatens the apple crop; Ada shows up at dawn to help and proves competent, unafraid of dirt. Working shoulder to shoulder, they fall into old rhythms. Emotional beat: the first thaw—Elias catching himself laughing and hating how good it feels.

chapters.title: The Developer's Dinner
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The developer courts Ada separately, offering to erase her debt and her past in one signature. At his gala she almost says yes—until she realizes she's rehearsing excuses the way she once rehearsed her apology. Emotional beat: the seduction of escape, refused.

chapters.title: What I Said at the Bus Stop
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A storm strands them in the kitchen with the journal open, and Ada finally speaks the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: why she left, what she was afraid of. Elias's anger cracks open into his own confession—he never stopped writing her letters he never sent. Emotional beat: catharsis, raw and unfinished.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The bank's appraiser values the orchard far below what they need; the refinance fails on paper. Elias, humiliated, pushes Ada away to spare her, and the developer moves to close. Emotional beat: the dark night—love against duty, with duty winning by the numbers.

chapters.title: The Supper Club Gambit
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ada and Elias bet everything on reopening the grandmother's kitchen for one night: a ticketed harvest supper using the journal's recipes, with proceeds and a story strong enough to bring a heritage-lending officer to the table. Emotional beat: two people choosing each other publicly, in front of the whole town.

chapters.title: The Kitchen of Junebug Creek
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The supper succeeds; the loan is approved, the deed is redrawn with both names intact—by choice this time. In the emptied kitchen, Ada and Elias write the first new page in the journal together. Emotional beat: resolution—memory no longer a weight but an inheritance they intend to spend.
